summary:
I have successfully found and resolved the issue.

### Root Cause
In `CsvReader.java`, the CSV files were being decoded using `ISO-8859-1` ("Latin-1") instead of `UTF-8`. Since the input CSV file `app/customers.csv` and the report output `ReportGenerator.java` both use UTF-8, this caused non-ASCII characters (like `é`, `ö`, `ü`, `ø`, etc.) to become corrupted during reading.

### Fix Applied
I updated `app/CsvReader.java` to use `StandardCharsets.UTF_8` instead of ISO-8859-1. 

### Verification
Running `./test.sh` rebuilt the codebase and successfully verified that all non-ASCII customer names and cities (including "Renée Duböis", "Hans Müller", "María García", "Søren Kirkegård", "François Léger", "Zoltán Kovács", "München", and "København") are preserved correctly without any corruption.
